source_text: ὁ ἄργυρος, ζωῆς δὲ ἡ σεμίδαλις, ὡς ἄρτου γένεσις τοῦ συνέχοντος εἰς ζωὴν, ἱλαρότητος δὲ τὸ ἔλαιον. Προσαγέσθω δὴ οὖν καὶ πρός γε ἡμῶν αὐτῶν τῷ ἐπὶ πάντων Θεῷ τὸ ὡς ἐν λαμπρότητι ζωῆς ἱλαρὸν, ἐλπίδι τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ. «Τῇ γὰρ ἐλπίδι χαίροντες,» φησί. Πῶς δ' ἂν εἶεν οὐχὶ τῆς ἀνωτάτω θυμηδίας ἔμπλεῳ, τὸ ἐν ζωῇ τε καὶ πολιτείᾳ περιφανὲς ἐξησκηκότες εὖ μάλα τῶν τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἐνταλμάτων οἱ φύλακες; οἷς πάντη τε καὶ πάντως τὸ ἐν μεθέξει γενέσθαι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ τεθησαύρισται παρὰ Θεῷ. «Ἀπεθάνετε γὰρ, φησὶ, καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν κέκρυπται σὺν τῷ Χριστῷ ἐν τῷ Θεῷ. Ὅταν ὁ Χριστὸς φανερωθῇ, ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν, τότε καὶ ὑμεῖς σὺν αὐτῷ φανερωθήσεσθε ἐν δόξῃ.» Οὐκοῦν ἡ σεμίδαλις ἐλαιόδευτος. Ἔνεστι γὰρ τῇ τῶν ἁγίων ζωῇ καὶ τὸ ὡς ἐν ἐλπίδι δόξης ἱλαρὸν, μετὰ λαμπρότητος δηλονότι τῆς ἐν ὁσιότητι καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ. Χρυσῆ δὲ θυΐσκη θυμιάματος πλήρης, τὸ τῶν ἁγίων γράφουσα κάλλος, καὶ ὡς ἐν σκεύεσιν ἐκλεκτοῖς τὸ εὐῶδες ἐν ἁγιασμῷ, εἶτα δῶρον ὥσπερ τι Θεῷ τὸ εὐοσμότατον ἀληθῶς. Ἢ οὐχὶ σκεύη λαμπρὰ καὶ ἀπόλεκτα τοὺς ἁγίους ὑπάρχειν οἰησαίμεθα ἂν, ὦ Παλλάδιε; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Μάλιστά γε. {ΚΥΡ.} Μόσχος δὲ ἦν παρ' ἑκάστου, καὶ δυοκαίδεκα μὲν οἱ πάντες. Ἀχθοφοροῦσί γε μὴν τὴν ἁγίαν σκηνὴν, κατὰ δύο προσενηνεγμένοι πρὸς ἅμαξαν μίαν, καὶ ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἕνα, ἐκνενέμηνται δὲ ταῖς τῶν Λευιτῶν ὑπουργίαις· καὶ τύπος ἂν εἴη τὸ χρῆμα τῶν δύο λαῶν, οὐκέτι μεμερισμένων εἰς ἀνομοιότητα δογμάτων καὶ ζωῆς, συνενηνεγμένοιν δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ συνδεδραμηκότοιν ὑπό γε τὸν ἕνα τοῦ Σωτῆρος ζυγὸν τληπαθῶς καὶ ἀνδρείως. «Ἀνδρίζου γὰρ, φησὶ, καὶ κραταιούσθω ἡ καρδία σου, καὶ ὑπόμεινον τὸν Κύριον.» Τληπαθὲς δὲ ζῶον ὁ μόσχος καὶ κραταιότατον. Τοιοίδε πάντως οἱ θεοσεβείας ᾑρημένοι, ζυγὸν ὥσπερ ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς ἐπέχοντες τὸν Χριστὸν, ὡς ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ προανατυπούμενον. Σῶμα δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ὁ θεῖος ἡμῖν ὠνόμαζε Παῦλος. Ἐλέγετο δὲ καὶ πρὸς Ἀνανίαν περὶ αὐτοῦ, φημὶ δὴ τοῦ Παύλου· «Πορεύου, ὅτι σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ἐστί μοι οὗτος, τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐναντίον τῶν ἐθνῶν.» Κριὸς δὲ πρὸς τούτοις, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀμνὸς τὰ προσενηνεγμένα, τοῦ τε πρεσβυτέρου προσενηνεγμένου καὶ τοῦ νέου λαοῦ τὴν πρὸς Θεὸν ἄφιξιν καὶ τὴν οἱονείπως ἀνάθεσιν, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τὴν πνευματικὴν, ὑπεμφαίνοντες. Ὥσπερ γὰρ τὸ τληπαθὲς καὶ ἀνδρεῖον ὡς ἔν γε τοῖς μόσχοις κατεσημαίνετο, κατὰ τὸν ἴσον, οἶμαι, τουτονὶ τρόπον καὶ ἐν τοῖς προβάτοις ἡ ὡς ἐν πραότητι καρποφορία τῶν διὰ πίστεως τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ δεδικαιωμένων διαδείκνυται σαφῶς. Πρᾶον γὰρ δὴ τὸ ζῶον, καὶ μὴν ἔγκαρπον. Τοιοῦτοι δὲ πάντες οἱ τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας ἀκριβεῖς ἐργάται, οἷς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπεφώνησεν ὁ Χριστός· «Παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ, μὴ ἀπαίτει, καὶ τῷ παίοντί σε εἰς τὴν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην.» Γράφει δὲ καὶ ὁ Παῦλος· «Δοῦλον δὲ Κυρίου οὐ δεῖ μάχεσθαι, ἀλλ' ἤπιον εἶναι
pass_a_gloss: [continuing §34: ‘and a symbol (σύμβολον) of brightness (λαμπρότης)’] the silver (ἄργυρος); and of life (ζωή) the fine flour (σεμίδαλις), as the origin (γένεσις) of bread that holds us together (συνέχω) into life; and of cheerfulness (ἱλαρότης) the oil (ἔλαιον). Let then be brought (προσάγω, imperative) also from us ourselves to the God over all the cheerful (ἱλαρός) as in brightness of life, by the hope (ἐλπίς) in Christ. ‘For rejoicing (χαίρω) in hope,’ he says. How would they not be full (ἔμπλεως) of the highest gladness (θυμηδία), the guardians (φύλακες) of the commandments (ἐντάλματα) of our Savior, who have practised (ἐξασκέω) very well the conspicuous (περιφανής) in life and conduct (πολιτεία)? For whom altogether and surely (πάντη τε καὶ πάντως) the coming into participation (μέθεξις) of his glory (δόξα) has been treasured up (θησαυρίζω, perfect) with God. ‘For you died, and your life has been hidden with Christ in God. When Christ is manifested (φανερόω), our life, then you also with him will be manifested in glory.’ Therefore the fine flour is oil-moistened (ἐλαιόδευτος). For there is in the life of the saints also the cheerful as in hope of glory, with brightness clearly, that in holiness (ὁσιότης) and righteousness (δικαιοσύνη). And a golden incense-dish (θυΐσκη) full of incense (θυμίαμα), depicting (γράφουσα) the beauty (κάλλος) of the saints, and as in chosen vessels (σκεύη ἐκλεκτά) the fragrance (τὸ εὐῶδες) in sanctification (ἁγιασμός), then as it were a gift (δῶρον) to God, the truly most fragrant (εὐοσμότατον). Or would we not think the saints to be bright and choice (ἀπόλεκτα) vessels, O Palladius? PALL.: Most certainly. CYR.: And a calf (μόσχος) was from each, twelve in all. They carry burdens (ἀχθοφορέω) for the holy tent (σκηνή), offered two to one wagon (ἅμαξα) and under one yoke (ζυγός), and have been assigned (ἐκνέμω) to the services (ὑπουργίαι) of the Levites; and the matter would be a type (τύπος) of the two peoples (λαοί), no longer divided into unlikeness (ἀνομοιότης) of doctrines (δόγματα) and life, but brought together (dual participles συνενηνεγμένοιν, συνδεδραμηκότοιν) and as it were run together under the one yoke of the Savior, enduringly (τληπαθῶς) and manfully (ἀνδρείως). ‘For be manly (ἀνδρίζομαι), and let your heart be strengthened (κραταιόω), and wait for (ὑπομένω) the Lord.’ And the calf is an enduring and very strong animal. Such altogether are those who have chosen godliness (θεοσέβεια), holding (ἐπέχω) Christ upon themselves like a yoke, as prefigured (προανατυπόω) in the holy tent. And the divine Paul named the Church his body (σῶμα). And it was said also to Ananias about him, I mean Paul: ‘Go, for this man is a vessel of choice (σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς) to me, to bear (βαστάζω) my name before the nations (ἔθνη).’ And a ram (κριός) besides these, and also a lamb (ἀμνός), the things offered, hinting (ὑπεμφαίνω) at the arrival (ἄφιξις) to God of the older (πρεσβύτερος) [‘offered’, προσενηνεγμένου, sic] and the new people, and as it were their dedication (ἀνάθεσις), clearly the spiritual one. For just as the enduring and manly was signified in the calves, in the equal manner, I think, also in the sheep (πρόβατα) the fruit-bearing (καρποφορία) as in meekness (πραότης) of those justified (δικαιόω) through faith in Christ is clearly shown. For the animal is meek and indeed fruitful (ἔγκαρπος). Such are all the exact workers (ἐργάται) of the Gospel conduct, to whom Christ himself proclaimed: ‘To everyone who asks you, give; and from him who takes your things, do not ask back; and to him who strikes you on the jaw (σιαγών), turn to him the other also.’ And Paul writes: ‘A slave (δοῦλος) of the Lord must not fight (μάχομαι), but be gentle (ἤπιος)… [continues in §36]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …is the silver; the fine flour is a symbol of life, since bread, which keeps us in life, is made from it; and the oil is a symbol of gladness. So let us too, for our part, offer to God who is over all, through our hope in Christ, the gladness that belongs to a bright life. For it says: ‘Rejoicing in hope’ (Romans 12:12). And how could those who keep the commandments of our Savior, and have trained themselves thoroughly in a life and conduct of shining distinction, not be filled with the highest joy? For them a share in his glory is stored up with God, wholly and surely. For it says: ‘For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ, our life, is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory’ (Colossians 3:3–4). So the fine flour is mixed with oil (Numbers 7:13). For in the life of the saints there is also the gladness that comes from the hope of glory, together, of course, with the brightness that belongs to holiness and righteousness. And the golden dish full of incense (Numbers 7:14) depicts the beauty of the saints: their fragrance in sanctification, held as in choice vessels, and then, as it were, a gift to God that is truly most fragrant. Or should we not think, Palladius, that the saints are bright and choice vessels?

Cyril: Each leader also gave an ox, twelve in all. They carry the holy tent as their load, brought in pairs to a single wagon and under a single yoke, and they were assigned to the service of the Levites (Numbers 7:3–6). This would be a type of the two peoples, no longer divided by unlike doctrines and ways of life, but brought together and, as it were, running together under the one yoke of the Savior (Matthew 11:29), with endurance and courage. For it says: ‘Be courageous, and let your heart be strong, and wait for the Lord’ (Psalm 27:14). And the ox is an animal that endures hardship and is very strong. Such, surely, are those who have chosen godliness: they carry Christ upon themselves like a yoke, as the one prefigured in the holy tent. The divine Paul, too, called the Church his body (Colossians 1:24). And it was said to Ananias about him, I mean about Paul: ‘Go, for this man is a chosen vessel to me, to carry my name before the Gentiles’ (Acts 9:15). Besides these, a ram and a lamb were offered (Numbers 7:15). They hint at the coming to God of the older people and of the new, and at their dedication, so to speak, which is plainly a spiritual one. For just as endurance and courage were signified in the oxen, so in the same way, I think, the sheep clearly show the fruit borne in meekness by those who have been justified through faith in Christ. For the animal is gentle, and fruitful as well. Such are all who labor with exactness at the Gospel way of life, to whom Christ himself said: ‘Give to everyone who asks you, and from the one who takes what is yours do not demand it back; and to the one who strikes you on the cheek, turn the other also’ (Luke 6:30; Matthew 5:39). And Paul too writes: ‘The Lord’s servant must not quarrel, but be gentle…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence: §34 ends ‘Σύμβολον δὲ λαμπρότητος μὲν’ (‘and a symbol of brightness’), so the English begins ‘…is the silver’ under Cyril’s label, following the convention of other Book 10 chunks. The silver dish and bowl were named in §34 (Numbers 7:13); the citation is placed here at the flour mixed with oil. θυΐσκη (Numbers 7:14 LXX) rendered ‘golden dish full of incense’ (NETS ‘censer’; English Bibles ‘dish’ or ‘pan’). σκηνή rendered ‘holy tent’, the term most Book 10 chunks and Book 3 use. μόσχος παρ’ ἑκάστου, δώδεκα: these are the twelve oxen drawing the six wagons, one ox from each leader, two leaders to a wagon (Numbers 7:3), given to the Levites for their service (Numbers 7:5–6); μόσχος rendered ‘ox’ because the animals pull wagons; Cyril then treats them as the calf of the offering list. Psalm 27:14 = LXX Psalm 26:14. ‘The one yoke of the Savior’ cited to Matthew 11:29 (‘take my yoke upon you’) as a clear allusion. ‘Paul called the Church his body’ cited to Colossians 1:24 (‘his body, which is the Church’); Ephesians 1:22–23 says the same. The quotation of Acts 9:15 is exact apart from word order. TEXTUAL FLAG: ‘τοῦ τε πρεσβυτέρου προσενηνεγμένου καὶ τοῦ νέου λαοῦ’ has a stray participle ‘offered’ attached to ‘the older’; the sense is clearly ‘of the older people and of the new’, and Pass B translates that sense; ram = older people (Israel), lamb = new people (from the Gentiles), parallel to the two peoples under one yoke. Luke 6:30; Matthew 5:39 (reviewer): the first two clauses are Luke 6:30 (παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει); the cheek clause ends with Matthew 5:39’s ‘στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην’ (Luke 6:29 has ‘πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην’), so the quotation blends the two and both are cited. The quotation of 2 Timothy 2:24–25 begins at the end of this section and finishes in §36, where the citation stands. Uncited: ‘choice vessels’ for the saints (cf. 2 Timothy 2:21; Acts 9:15 follows) and ‘fragrance’ (cf. 2 Corinthians 2:15) are too loose for a citation.

changes: untangled ‘offer to the God who is over all the gladness’ (garden path); hope now governs the gladness as in the Greek
‘trained themselves well… that shine out’ -> ‘trained themselves thoroughly in a life and conduct of shining distinction’ (εὖ μάλα, περιφανές)
ἁγιασμός ‘holiness’ -> ‘sanctification’ (ὁσιότης already ‘holiness’); εἶτα ‘and so’ -> ‘and then’; ‘most sweet-smelling’ -> ‘most fragrant’
ἀχθοφοροῦσι τὴν σκηνήν: ‘carry the load of’ -> ‘carry the holy tent as their load’; κατὰ δύο -> ‘in pairs’
‘The thing would be’ -> ‘This would be’; τληπαθῶς καὶ ἀνδρείως no longer expanded to ‘enduring hardship with patience and courage’
θεοσέβεια ‘the fear of God’ -> ‘godliness’; ὑπεμφαίνοντες ‘show’ -> ‘hint at’; ἀκριβεῖς ἐργάται ‘faithfully’ -> ‘with exactness’
Luke 6:29–30 -> Luke 6:30; Matthew 5:39 (cheek clause uses Matthew’s στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην); bible_refs and note updated
